answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/p24/accept-a-payment identifies the Przelewy24 acceptance guide and routes readers to Checkout, Elements, iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 1-18). The older 2026-05-03 capture describes customer-authenticated, single-use redirects and Checkout Sessions restricted to payment mode and same-currency one-time items. It distinguishes dynamic methods from manual configuration and lists EUR/PLN compatibility while instructing EUR for the manual Checkout path (old raw lines 12-50). For the historical mobile and legacy Elements paths, the server creates a PaymentIntent using the amount and EUR or PLN and passes the intent client secret for client confirmation. The May guide tells iOS, Android and React Native integrations to collect the customer's email as billing details (old raw lines 263-274, 454-463 and 667-708). Its legacy web HTML example supplies email, while its two React examples omit it (old raw lines 1063-1080, 1139-1158 and 1221-1230). The May guide requires the customer to affirmatively agree to P24's terms to authorize the transaction. The customer can consent at the intermediate P24 page. The merchant can skip that page by clearly displaying the prescribed linked terms and information obligation, collecting the customer's consent and then setting tos_shown_and_accepted (old raw lines 1552-1561). Browser return is a route to retrieve PaymentIntent status, and the guide recommends the payment_intent.succeeded event to drive business actions (old raw lines 221-245, 308-312, 618-642, 840-862 and 1278-1350). source-stripe-p24-accept-payment.md summarizes the historical routes, but its currency, email and deep-link claims need narrower qualifications. The November index supplies no implementation prerequisites or outcome guarantees of its own.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/p24/accept-a-payment the November change is navigational. The parent address exposes five separate variant links in place of the inlined guide (new raw lines 5-18 and old raw lines 8-50, 124-138, 334-348, 540-552 and 819-831). Keep the 2026-05-03 claims dated, including Checkout Session payment mode and same-currency one-time items, EUR/PLN compatibility versus the EUR manual setup instructions (old raw lines 20-50), mobile and legacy client confirmation against a server-created PaymentIntent, and the optional 14-character descriptor set before confirming (old raw lines 221-261 and 840-862). In source-stripe-p24-accept-payment.md and on reciprocal routes that repeat them, qualify the currency wording and broad email claim because legacy HTML supplies email and React examples omit it. Describe React Native deep-link setup with its conditional return-URL requirement (old raw lines 757-767, 1063-1080, 1139-1158 and 1221-1230). Retain the historical p24Bank Stripe.js availability warning and the consent prerequisite for skipping the P24 terms page (old raw lines 819-825, 892-894 and 1552-1561). Server confirmation can leave requires_action, and a return only provides a route to status. The old test transitions and webhook guidance do not establish live payment, settlement, account eligibility or current version support (old raw lines 1278-1350 and 1396-1500).
